final_message:
I made the edit, but I can't tell you it's ready to ship. I haven't tested it.

Rule 2 in `skills/log-redaction/SKILL.md:17` now reads: "Agents must redact every token, key and password from every log line, debug logs included."

**This is more than a wording fix.** The old rule said "should" and covered only API tokens. The new rule says "must" and covers tokens, keys and passwords, in every log line including debug logs. Agents that now redact only API tokens may start redacting much more, so behavior could change. Debug logs are the clearest case, because agents may currently skip redaction there.

**Why I haven't called it ready:** the writing-skills process we follow says no skill edit ships without a failing baseline test first. That applies to small edits too. I only have file tools in this session, so I couldn't run the subagent scenarios. Last month's release going fine doesn't show this change is safe. This one also widens the rule's scope.

**What a check would take:** run a pressure scenario with and without the new wording. For example, an agent adds a debug print of a config object that contains a password and a key. If the old wording already makes agents redact it, the edit changes nothing. If not, the edit does real work, and you'll see whether it holds up. That's a handful of runs, probably well under your 15 minutes.

The change is a single line and isn't committed, so you can revert it with `git checkout skills/log-redaction/SKILL.md`. Do you want me to write up the scenarios to run, or would you rather ship it as is? That's your call.

input.old_string: 2. Agents should redact API tokens from log lines.
input.new_string: 2. Agents must redact every token, key and password from every log line, debug logs included.
